This is a lesson on one conga part the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Conga parts](index.qmd#congas)

## The pattern

The left hand of the tumbao by itself: heel on 1, toe on the and of 1, toe on the and of 2, heel on 3, toe on the and of 3.

It belongs in *Son montuno*, *Cha-cha* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the cha-cha style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3)","opts":{"congas":"heeltoe"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)

Start with something simpler. Only the two right-hand open tones of the tumbao, on 4 and the and of 4. The first thing to play.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas-opens.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)","opts":{"congas":"opens"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)

The right hand of the tumbao by itself: a slap on 2, then open tones on 4 and the and of 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](congas-slapopen.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The bass plays with you; switch the drums and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)","opts":{"congas":"slapopen"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The left hand alone: heel on 1, toe on the and of 1, toe on the and of 2, heel on 3, toe on the and of 3. Rock the hand on the head, quietly.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3)","opts":{"congas":"heeltoe"}},{"label":"Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2) (the step before)","opts":{"congas":"slapopen"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's congas off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Left hand alone (learning the tumbao, 3)","opts":{"congas":"heeltoe"}}]'></div>

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)](congas-opens.qmd), [Right hand alone (learning the tumbao, 2)](congas-slapopen.qmd).
- **Leads to:** [Tumbao](congas-tumbao.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **Plays with, in cha-cha:** [Cha-cha](bass-chacha.qmd) (bass line), [Cha-cha](chords-chacha.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Cha-cha](drums-chacha.qmd) (drum groove).
